features.behavior: One process-wide engine owns independent PTY-backed terminal sessions.
features.linux_acceptance: Create, pump, resize, write to, observe child exit from, and close 20 independent sessions without leaked children or file descriptors.
features.translation: Use Linux PTY/process semantics; no AppKit dependency.

features.behavior: Child output mutates the screen, text extraction reflects it, and damage schedules a redraw.
features.linux_acceptance: A deterministic child command appears in extracted UTF-8 and fires damage without polling the GUI.

features.behavior: A live terminal session renders through Kitty's OpenGL pipeline inside a host-owned framebuffer.
features.linux_acceptance: GtkGLArea renders a live shell, resizes without session loss, restores host GL state, reports visible initialization failures, and closes without a live child.
features.linux_status: Slice 2.1 passed on GTK 4.22.4 over X11 with Mesa llvmpipe on 2026-07-24; Wayland, physical GPU, fractional scale, and input remain open.
features.translation: The GUI process isolates libpython but uses distro native graphics/text libraries to avoid loader collisions with GTK.

features.behavior: Keyboard protocol encoding, raw writes, bracketed paste, and composed text reach only the focused pane.
features.linux_acceptance: GTK key events, paste, dead keys, emoji, and an IME commit produce the expected child bytes on Wayland and X11.
features.linux_status: Slices 2.2A and 2.2B are closed: GDK press/release/repeat routing, kitty's encoder over live DECCKM and keyboard-protocol state, focus transfer to an adjacent GTK control, and a real GtkIMContext covering Compose, dead keys, AltGr, a non-US layout, emoji, and an IBus preedit/commit flow all pass over X11 against fixed byte expectations. Paste, clipboard, and Wayland remain unproven, and input-method evidence covers one Latin conversion engine rather than a CJK engine with candidate windows.
features.translation: Map GDK key/modifier values to the stable libkitty key contract.

features.behavior: Each session independently owns scrollback, selection, extracted text, and search markers.
features.linux_acceptance: Two sessions retain independent scroll, selection, and search state across focus changes.
features.linux_status: Headless libkitty APIs are covered; GTK selection, scrolling, and search wiring are unproven.

features.behavior: Selection, terminal mouse reporting, wheel routing, and URL hit-testing use visible terminal cells.
features.linux_acceptance: Pointer coordinates remain correct at 100%, 150%, and 200% scale; Shift preserves local selection and scrolling.
features.linux_status: GTK pointer, wheel, URL, and scale-coordinate behavior is unproven.
features.translation: Never assume Retina or a fixed backing scale.

features.behavior: Workspaces own groups, groups own tabs, and tabs own stable pane IDs and split trees.
features.linux_acceptance: Create, select, rename, reorder where supported, and close hierarchy nodes while preserving stable IDs and the non-empty root invariants.
features.translation: Implement as pure Rust before binding GTK widgets.

features.behavior: Nested horizontal and vertical splits preserve ratios, focus, minimum sizes, and deterministic close order.
features.linux_acceptance: Frozen split fixtures produce the same leaf order, divider ownership, ratio clamping, focus successor, and collapse result.
features.translation: GTK layout is a projection; it must not own the split model.

features.behavior: Crash-safe JSON restores hierarchy, IDs, split ratios, selected nodes, safe cwd, and approved metadata into fresh sessions.
features.linux_acceptance: Valid v1 fixtures round-trip; malformed/oversized/duplicate-ID input is rejected or repaired identically; loading never executes resume commands.
features.translation: Use XDG state paths and atomic replace plus fsync semantics.

features.behavior: Bounded terminal font, color, opacity, padding, close-confirmation, and scroll settings have stable defaults.
features.linux_acceptance: Portable settings fixtures decode to the same values and invalid values fall back per schema.
features.translation: Exclude macOS window chrome, launch-at-login, and shortcut representations.

features.behavior: Closing a pane or parent scope warns when a protected foreground job would be terminated and rechecks before acting.
features.linux_acceptance: Foreground, stopped foreground, and background-only job cases match the fixture matrix; closing reaps every descendant without zombies.
features.translation: Validate against Linux job-control behavior, not Darwin assumptions.

features.behavior: Copy/paste uses the desktop clipboard and terminal notifications surface through the OS service.
features.linux_acceptance: Clipboard and freedesktop notifications work under both Wayland and X11 without blocking terminal pumping.
features.linux_status: GTK clipboard belongs to Slice 2.2; notifications and Wayland remain later and unproven.
features.translation: Portal behavior must be tested in sandboxed packages.

features.behavior: A bounded versioned local control protocol addresses stable hierarchy IDs and never trusts ambient callers.
features.linux_acceptance: Unix-socket framing, peer ownership, request/response limits, method IDs, and error codes pass shared fixtures.
features.translation: Use SO_PEERCRED and mode 0600; do not copy Darwin credential code.

features.behavior: Saved SSH profiles expose reviewed host aliases and reconnect only after explicit user action.
features.linux_acceptance: Portable profile fixtures validate and render an argv preview; fixture import and snapshot restore never connect.
features.translation: Resolve executable and config through Linux PATH and user config.

features.behavior: Browser surfaces share pane containers with terminal surfaces.
features.linux_acceptance: Only after explicit approval, WebKitGTK surfaces preserve stable pane/surface IDs and isolation without degrading terminal performance.
features.linux_status: No browser feature work is authorized. Slice 2.3 requires only a minimal coexistence probe before the toolkit decision.

features.behavior: AppKit titlebar, Dock, Services, AppleScript, code signing, and macOS login-item behavior.
features.linux_acceptance: No direct parity claim; Linux replacements require separate feature IDs and acceptance tests.
features.translation: Use freedesktop/XDG equivalents only where product value justifies them.
